# Events generated by two partition atoms

*Easy · [Probability problems](index.md)*

On $\Omega=\{1,2,3,4\}$, how many events belong to the sigma-algebra generated by the partition $\{1\},\{2,3,4\}$?

```answer
{"answer":{"kind":"integer","expected":"4","checker_scope":"Checks the number of events in this generated information sigma-algebra only."}}
```

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Events in a partition-generated sigma-algebra are unions of whole partition atoms.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Each of the two atoms is either included or excluded. List the resulting distinct unions.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Worked solution</summary>

A two-atom information structure has one event for each atom subset.

1. The two nonempty disjoint atoms cover $\Omega$; a generated event cannot separate points inside an atom.
2. The possible unions are $\varnothing$, $\{1\}$, $\{2,3,4\}$ and $\Omega$.
3. These four events already form a sigma-algebra containing the partition, so they are exactly the generated sigma-algebra. The count is four, not the full power-set count sixteen.

Empty, first atom, second atom and whole space are the four generated events.

</details>
